features.note: Two wire families at +-45 deg on a 50 mm aperture at the true 4.9 mm gauge. The partition stays SEE-THROUGH at the 3/4 hero angle: the stored pallets, their wooden decks and the interior posts are all legible through it, and the grazing view shows the wires still reading as separate members instead of piling into a wall. This is the failure datacenter/rack-servidores paid for with 10 mm-deep bars.

Reads as painted green enamel with no metal glint, against a single bare-metal padlock — the contrast is what makes the dielectric read as a dielectric. Measured anchor [17,67,46] at deviation 0.00 on the +X corner post; dE00 0 vs the declared target.
All nine posts land on dark shoes over 225 mm base plates; the gap between the bottom panel frame and the floor is legible across the whole footprint in the hero view, including the far corners.

Framed 600x450 opening with its shelf on two brackets, and the opening genuinely reads as a HOLE: the back-wall mesh seen through it renders at a visibly finer pitch than the front panel around it, and a stored carton shows through. The shelf reads brighter than its dark albedo (see defects).

Lowest-scoring critical feature and the honest one. The framed opening, the reinforced hinge stile and the hasp+padlock are all present and correct; the padlock reads unambiguously as a padlock (body, smooth shackle arc, keyway) ONLY in the native-resolution crop. At hero scale it is a small pale mark. Present and correct, but it carries its identity at 1:1, not at a glance.

important_features.note: Continuous bar over the top frames along the full perimeter, visible against the dark background on all four runs.
Three pallets with unit loads, placed clear of the door approach; they are what proves the 82% open area is a real property and not a claim.

defects: The service shelf renders at [180,181,181] — near-white — although its albedo is dark grey #3a4046. Its top face is nearly horizontal and takes the key almost head-on, so it is the brightest object in the frame and pulls the eye off the door. Not clipped, and physically coherent (the grazing view shows the same shelf dark from below), but it over-reads.

The roof panel is effectively unseen: at the hero elevation (13 deg) it is edge-on, and no shot in the evidence set frames it. It is measurably present (168 wire instances, visible=true) but nothing in the captures would let a reviewer confirm the cage is CLOSED on top — which is part of what makes it a secure store rather than a fence.

The door leaf carries the same aperture and the same enamel as the wall panels, so at hero scale the leaf separates from the partition only by its frame. Correct per the source (the leaf is the same mesh), but it costs the door some legibility.

mechanical.note: Console-clean read from BOTH capture sidecars (?view=neutral and ?view=grazing), each console_clean:true with an empty issues array. probe.mjs medians 27 draws / 14666 tris against a perf_budget of 40 / 200000; fps ignored (informational only under SwiftShader). No test suite exists for this design, so tests is null rather than fabricated. colorTarget authored from this same gated capture (the kit's golden-render path, since no reference photograph exists) and re-measured through material-color-probe.mjs: dE00 0, pass true. THREE DEVIATIONS FROM THE GATE CONTRACT, recorded rather than hidden: (1) the reviewer is the ORCHESTRATOR INLINE, not a fresh-context blind agent — this session is not permitted to spawn subagents, and GATES.md allows an inline role hat only in quick mode, so this verdict is a SELF-REVIEW and is NOT the independent acceptance authority the contract requires; it should be re-reviewed blind before the asset is treated as contract-passed. (2) The `neutral` evidence view is deliberately identical to the default camera (it is the hero framing); the distinctness check therefore proves neutral vs grazing differ, not that neutral differs from default. (3) No `reference-match` view exists because this design has NO reference photographs — evidence is a textual federal specification (spec p6_comparison: spec-only). Two design defects were caught by the ORCHESTRATOR PRE-LOOK before this attempt's review was written, and fixed: the padlock rendered as a flat black silhouette (bare metal on a vertical face whose mirror ray hits the dark floor — fixed by a practical placed on the solved reflection direction, never by lowering metalness), and its hasp/body/shackle merged into one pale slab with a stair-stepped arc at 8x16 torus segments. Both were invisible in the downscaled frame and visible only in a native-resolution crop.
